feeds.title: Jessie Rasche Blog
feeds.description: Jessie Rasche, a professional artist based in Brookings, paints in her home studio and rural landscapes. Her work graces private collections worldwide and public spaces like hospitals and government buildings. As an award-winning member of prestigious art societies, her talent is recognized by Southwest Art Magazine and featured in prominent publications.

feeds.title: Rapid City Arts Council News
feeds.description: Established in 1968, Rapid City Arts Council champions art's unifying power, enhancing accessibility and inspiration. They envision a world where art serves as a universal language, fostering connections and igniting creativity. Through community engagement, they rally support for the transformative potential of art.

feeds.title: Redlin Art Center Blog
feeds.description: The Redlin Art Center, nestled in Watertown, SD, showcases over 160 original oil paintings by artist Terry Redlin. It's a heartfelt gift from Redlin to his hometown, celebrating family, nature, and fine arts. Each exhibit tells Redlin's story, inviting visitors to connect with his passions and inspirations. Explore the centre to delve into Redlin's work and legacy.

feeds.title: Piper Arts Blog
feeds.description: The Piper Arts blog showcases regional artists, highlights community art events, and shares insights into custom framing and art installations, reflecting the vibrant art scene in Sioux Falls.

feeds.title: Visit Brookings » Arts
feeds.description: Founded in 1982 as a Chamber committee, the Brookings Convention and Visitors Bureau became an organization in 2020. It separated from the Chamber to prioritize the visitor industry. With vibrant murals, sculptures, and hands-on classes, art flourishes in Brookings, enhancing its appeal as a destination.

feeds.title: TENYOH | My Thoughts
feeds.description: Inheriting Tenyoh, the artist embraces its profound meaning: an ocean from a mountaintop. With a background in international healthcare, they value emotional connections over cultural differences. Their art transcends specific groups, portraying human nature's complexities through ceramic sculpting while retaining a consistent thematic focus.
